name: Sota Ritual (Bitter Waters)
notes: Detailed procedure of the sota rite: warning, seclusion, scroll writing, erasing in water, drinking the bitter waters, and its effects

name: Warning (Kinui) for Sota
notes: Specific rules for issuing a valid warning (kinui) to one's wife prohibiting seclusion with a named man, number of witnesses required, and its effects

name: Seclusion (Stiha/Hastarah) in Sota
notes: Rules regarding the prohibited seclusion that triggers the sota process: duration, witnesses required, and what constitutes sufficient seclusion

name: Erasing the Scroll (Mechikat HaMegillah)
notes: Laws of writing and erasing the sota scroll into the bitter waters: materials permitted, passages written, and conditions that invalidate the scroll

name: Merit Delaying Sota Punishment
notes: Debate whether personal merit can delay or prevent the sotah water's effects, and implications for teaching daughters Torah

name: Sota Meal-Offering (Minchat Kena'ot)
notes: Specific rules distinguishing the sota's barley meal-offering from other meal-offerings: no oil, no frankincense, brought in wicker basket, Egyptian basket

name: Measure for Measure (Midah k'Neged Midah)
notes: Principle that Divine punishment and reward correspond proportionally to a person's actions, illustrated through sota, Samson, Absalom, Miriam, Joseph, Moses

name: Recitations Valid in Any Language
notes: Category of Torah recitations and declarations (e.g., Shema, Amidah, Birkat Hamazon, vow oaths) that may be said in any language, not only Hebrew

name: Recitations Required in Hebrew (Lashon haKodesh)
notes: Category of Torah recitations that must specifically be said in Hebrew: bikkurim declaration, chalitza, blessings and curses at Gerizim/Ebal, priestly blessing, High Priest's Yom Kippur reading, Hakhel, eglah arufah, war priest's address

name: Bikkurim Declaration (Mikra Bikkurim)
notes: The specific verbal declaration recited when bringing first fruits to the Temple, required in Hebrew, and its textual content (Deuteronomy 26)

name: Hakhel (Assembly at Sukkot)
notes: The septennial public Torah reading by the king at Sukkot following the Sabbatical Year: procedure, Torah portions read, blessings recited, and King Agrippa episode

name: Priest Anointed for War (Kohen Mashuach Milchama)
notes: The special priest appointed to address soldiers before battle, his speech in Hebrew, and his role in war preparations

name: War Exemptions (Petur miMilchama)
notes: Categories of men exempt from military service: new house not dedicated, vineyard not yet used, betrothed not yet married; distinction between obligatory and elective wars

name: Obligatory vs. Elective War (Milchemet Mitzvah/Reshut)
notes: Distinction between obligatory wars (milchemet mitzvah) where no exemptions apply and elective wars (milchemet reshut) where biblical exemptions for new house, vineyard, and betrothal apply

name: Eglah Arufah Procedure
notes: Detailed procedure of the broken-necked heifer ritual: measurement from corpse to nearest city, who goes out, nachal eitan, elders' declaration, priests' recitation

name: Nachal Eitan (Perennial Stream for Eglah Arufah)
notes: Requirement that the heifer be brought to a perennial or forceful stream; whether this requirement is indispensable or not

name: Blessings and Curses at Gerizim and Ebal
notes: The ceremony of blessings and curses pronounced on Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal: who stood where, procedure of Levites turning and reciting, the people's Amen responses

name: High Priest's Torah Reading on Yom Kippur
notes: Procedure for the High Priest reading Torah portions on Yom Kippur, the blessings recited afterward, and the order of passing the scroll

name: High Priest's Blessings on Yom Kippur
notes: The eight blessings recited by the High Priest on Yom Kippur after the Torah reading: Torah, Temple service, thanksgiving, forgiveness, Temple, Israel, priests, Jerusalem

name: Nullification of Sota Waters (Bitul Mei Sotah)
notes: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai's nullification of the sota bitter water ritual when adultery proliferated among men, based on Hosea 4:14

name: Shamir Worm
notes: The legendary shamir worm used to cut the Temple stones without iron; said to have ceased after the Second Temple's destruction

name: Takkanot of Yochanan the High Priest
notes: Enactments attributed to Yochanan the High Priest: abolishing tithe declaration, nullifying awakeners and strikers at Temple, and demai inquiry

name: Footsteps of the Messiah (Ikveta diMeshicha)
notes: Signs and characteristics of the pre-Messianic era: moral deterioration, disrespect for elders, erosion of faith and family bonds, impudence

name: Pinchas ben Yair's Ladder of Virtues
hebrew: סולם של רבי פינחס בן יאיר
notes: The ascending chain of spiritual virtues from Torah study through diligence, cleanliness, purity, piety, humility, fear of sin, holiness, divine spirit, to resurrection

name: Tithe Confession/Declaration (Viduy Maaser)
notes: The formal declaration recited after the third and sixth years of the Sabbatical cycle confirming proper distribution of tithes; may be recited in any language per Mishnah Sotah

name: Teaching Daughters Torah
notes: Debate between Ben Azzai (obligation to teach daughters Torah) and Rabbi Eliezer (teaching daughters Torah is tiflut/promiscuity)

name: Sota Forbidden to Paramour
notes: The prohibition on the sota woman marrying her paramour after divorce, derived from the double expression of defilement in Numbers 5

name: Priest's Address Before Battle (Divrei Kohen)
notes: The specific speech given by the war-priest to soldiers before battle, expounding Deuteronomy 20:3-4, encouraging soldiers against fear of enemy weapons and sounds

name: Levite City Boundaries (Migrash Arei Levi)
notes: Interpretation of the 1000 vs 2000 cubit measurements around Levite cities (Numbers 35:4-5): one for open land, one for fields/vineyards or Shabbat boundary

name: Manner of Singing the Song at the Sea
notes: Debate whether Israel sang the Song of the Sea responsively after Moses (like Hallel) or in unison together with Moses (like Shema)
